messages:
maya: Nightly CI flagged a kernel selection regression on aarch64 A100 runs for long sequences (>2048). perf-bot posted the artifact :eyes:
perf-bot: nightly-run 1762501200 results uploaded: https://ci.internal/runs/1762501200 · summary: +12% p50 latency on gen for seq=4096, candidate kernel set changed to 'k-v2' on that arch
ajay: Hmm, autotuner picked k-v2 because it beats on short seqs but is slower on long streams. Did the autotuner weight latency vs. throughput differently for that arch?
maya: I checked the autotune snapshot — it used the default cost model, and the seq distribution was skewed to <512 for that customer workload sample. So pick makes sense statistically but regresses our long-seq path.
devon: This smells like our sequence-length-dependent dispatch isn't testing tails. We should add a microbenchmark that exercises 1k/2k/4k seqs on both k-v1 and k-v2 on A100 and Ampere variants.
sam: Agreed. I can add a small harness entry. Proposed command:
```
./tools/kernel_bench --model gpt2-xl --kernel-candidates k-v1,k-v2 --seq-lens 128,512,1024,2048,4096 --batch-sizes 1,4 --arch a100 --kv-cache on --runs 20 --out json
```
maya: Perfect. Also capture continuous-batching pressure: include flags --enable-cont-batch --target-latency 50ms
ajay: For CI gating, we should fail if p50 regression >5% for any seq bucket and arch. Also capture p95 and tail distribution.
devon: I'll add a regression test that pins the kernel mapping for the canary and asserts no regressed buckets. If autotuner suggests a new mapping, we surface as a PR but don't auto-accept for prod.
perf-bot: added test harness job: kernel-candidate-smoke-a100 (cron nightly). Artifacts: s3://perf-artifacts/1762501200/{kbench.json,profiles/}
maya: Can someone triage the raw profile? I saw increased memcpy in the k-v2 path for large KV cache states.
sam: Repro steps I used locally:
1) docker run -it --gpus all --rm rwdn/kbench:latest
2) /bin/bash -c "./kbench --model gpt2-xl --kernel k-v2 --seq-len 4096 --kv-cache on --batch 1 --runs 50 --trace"
Output snippet:
"p50: 210ms, p95: 320ms, memcpy-time: 72ms (KV-copy)"
ajay: That memcpy spike looks like the kernel moved KV to an intermediate buffer for alignment. Maybe alignment heuristics differ by arch.
maya: Short-term mitigation: add sequence-length split in kernel selector: if seq >= 2048, prefer k-v1 on a100 family. We'll add a whitelist policy in the selector config and run canary.
devon: Long-term: autotuner should include a seq-tail penalty in its objective or include histograms per-workload. Also incorporate KV-state size into the cost model.
sam: I'll open a small PR with the harness test and selector override. Link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/4982
maya: Thanks. After merge, let's let the nightly run for 3 days then flip the autotuner suggestion tooling to show diffs in Slack.
ajay: Also add a note to release docs: "kernel selection: sequence-length heuristics adjusted for A100 long-seq workloads" so oncall knows the change.
perf-bot: CI job kernel-candidate-smoke-a100 completed: 1762504800 · status: flaky 1/3 runs failed (regression detected).
maya: OK let's keep this thread open until we have canary numbers. Thanks all :thumbsup:
